output.title: Late payment terms are a workflow problem, not just a finance problem
output.body:
Late payment terms usually show up first as a workflow problem, not a finance problem. For an owner-operator, the useful question is not “are the terms bad?” but “which repeating task is creating the drag: invoice tracking, payment-chasing emails, or an aging report in a spreadsheet?” That is the bounded decision worth looking at first.

If the task is repeatable, measurable, and mostly the same each time, it may be a good candidate for AI or workflow automation. If it changes too much from case to case, or if it touches money movement, keep human approval in place and leave the high-risk step manual. That is not a failure; it is just control.

Bareni’s normal sequence is a free diagnostic, then a one-page pilot proposal, then a working MVP if the workflow fits. Those timings are intended scopes, not guarantees, and the diagnostic can honestly say AI is not the right fit.

A practical next step: look at the last five overdue-payment cases and ask one question about each one — was the follow-up basically the same every time? If yes, you have a workflow to examine. If no, you probably have a judgment call that stays human. Dry, but useful.
